findings.title: A `coroutine<T>` named only in a data position (struct field / array element / generic type argument) emits `extc_coro` without ever emitting its typedef: the generated C does not compile
findings.why: `cType()` renders every `coroutine<T>` as the runtime handle `extc_coro` (src/codegen.c:482 for TY_STRUCT and :495 for TY_GENERIC), but the typedef `struct ExtcCoroS`/`extc_coro` is emitted only when the flag `g.needCoroHandle` is set (src/codegen.c:7072-7076). The only places that set it are the box-coercion prepass (`if (cf->coroBoxed) g.needCoroHandle = true;`, src/codegen.c:6779) and handle-expression sites (:1873, :2136, :2342, :2372, :2389, :3804, :3824). A type that is merely *mentioned* (struct field, array element, generic type argument) never passes through any of them, so the field type is emitted and its definition is not. The checker accepts the program, so this is the generator dropping a definition it still references.
findings.trigger: Any accepted program that names `coroutine<T>` in a data position and never boxes a frame (no assignment of a coroutine call result to a handle-typed destination). Minimal: `struct holder { h: coroutine<i64>  n: i64 }` + a `main` that only stores `n`. Also reproduces for `[2]coroutine<i64>` array elements and for `box<coroutine<i64>>`.

cd /tmp/rev/genwarn && /home/alphayang/extC_Compiler/build/extc -w g1_coro_field.extc -o g1_coro_field.c   # rc=0, accepted
$ gcc -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused -fsyntax-only g1_coro_field.c
g1_coro_field.c:115:5: error: unknown type name 'extc_coro'
  115 |     extc_coro h;
      |     ^~~~~~~~~
$ clang -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused -fsyntax-only g1_coro_field.c
g1_coro_field.c:115:5: error: unknown type name 'extc_coro'
1 error generated.
(Also hit in the corpus: stdlib/std/coro/scheduler.extc -> /tmp/rev/gen/stdlib__std__coro__scheduler.c:140:5 error.)

findings.title: Zero value of a generic instance whose type argument is `coroutine<T>` is emitted as `(extc_coro){ .unit = false }` - a designator for a field the real handle type does not have
findings.why: `zeroValue()` has two representations for the same type. For a TY_GENERIC instance it spells the zero out field by field (src/codegen.c:1560-1579, the designator is built at :1574) instead of using the `{0}` shortcut taken by the TY_STRUCT branch (:1582-1585, guarded by needsExplicitZero). `coroutine<T>` is itself an instance of the prelude's marker struct `struct coroutine<A, B> { unit: bool }` (stdlib/prelude.extc:43-45), so spelling it out produces `.unit = false`, while `cType()` makes the container field an `extc_coro` (src/codegen.c:482/495) whose real definition is `struct ExtcCoroS { void *frame; int64_t kind; int64_t task; }` (:7075). Type and initializer come from two different representations, so the C is rejected. needsExplicitZero already answers false for such a field, so only the TY_GENERIC branch's unconditional spelling is at fault.
findings.trigger: A generic struct instantiated with a coroutine type argument, in a program that also sets needCoroHandle (so the real typedef is present): `var c: box<coroutine<i64>>` where `box<T>` is a user generic struct and a coroutine handle is boxed somewhere. Without the boxing, the program fails earlier for the missing typedef (finding 1).

findings.title: A `dyn Trait` used only in a data position (struct field / array element / generic type argument) emits `ExtcDynHandle` without emitting its typedef
findings.why: TY_DYN is rendered as the runtime handle `ExtcDynHandle` (src/codegen.c:491), and the handle's definition is emitted only under `if (m->usesDyn)` (src/codegen.c:7065-7070, and the runtime at :8461). `usesDyn` is a checker-level flag set when a dyn *value* is produced, not when the dyn *type* is named, so any program that stores dyn values in a field/array/type argument but never constructs one gets a struct field of an undefined type. The same program with one `dyn Tag(...)` expression anywhere compiles, which isolates the flag as the missing trigger.
findings.trigger: A dyn type in a data position with no dyn value built: `struct box<T> { v: T }` + `var b: box<dyn Tag>`; equally `struct holder { d: dyn Tag  n: i64 }` and `var a: [2]dyn Tag`. Control: adding `let d = dyn Tag(bx { v: i64(3) })` makes the same program compile cleanly.

findings.title: -Warray-bounds on generated `__extc_a[3]` with an `extc_arena[2]` declaration: a domain block nested inside an `if` walks off the frame arena array (ASan-confirmed stack-buffer-overflow)
findings.code_quote:
/* generated (g4_arena_bounds.c), with #line mapping to the .extc source */
    extc_arena __extc_a[2] = {0};                 /* line 941: sized 1 + blkMaxOfBlock(body) */
...
#line 13 "g4_arena_bounds.extc"
            extc_arena_release(&__extc_a[3]);     /* line 954: index 3 into [2] */

/* gcc -c -O2: */
g4_arena_bounds.extc:13:13: warning: array subscript 3 is above array bounds of 'extc_arena[2]' [-Warray-bounds=]
   13 |       ext task(i64(2), i64(1))
findings.why: The frame arena array is sized by `maxLv = 1 + blkMaxOfBlock(f->body)` (src/codegen.c:4715) and emitted as `extc_arena __extc_a[maxLv + 1]` (:4763), so its size depends on blkMaxLevel() counting every statement that opens a block level. blkMaxLevel() (:3642-3667) handles ST_BLOCK, ST_IF, ST_WHILE and ST_MATCH and returns 0 for everything else (default: at :3665) - ST_DOMAIN (`d.run { ... }`) is not handled, so every block inside a domain block is invisible to the sizing pass while genBlockBody still assigns it a level (cgReleaseLevel emits `extc_arena_release(&__extc_a[lvl])` at :3391). `d.run { if ... { ext ... } }` therefore needs level 3 in an array sized 2. This is the same root cause as the already-reported `__extc_a[2]` overrun in tests/ext/domain_runs.extc; what is new here is that one more nesting level makes it a full subscript-past-the-end that the C compiler itself reports (and not only a one-past-the-end `&a[n]`), plus an ASan-confirmed read.
findings.trigger: A `d.run { ... }` block containing any nested block (e.g. `if`) that itself contains an arena-using operation, e.g. `ext <coro>(...)` or an allocation. One nesting level inside the domain block is enough to go from index 2 (one-past-end) to index 3 (past-the-end).
findings.repro:
cd /tmp/rev/genwarn && /home/alphayang/extC_Compiler/build/extc -w g4_arena_bounds.extc -o g4_arena_bounds.c   # rc=0, accepted
$ gcc -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused -c -o /dev/null g4_arena_bounds.c
g4_arena_bounds.extc: In function 'main':
g4_arena_bounds.extc:13:13: warning: array subscript 3 is above array bounds of 'extc_arena[2]' [-Warray-bounds=]
   13 |       ext task(i64(2), i64(1))
g4_arena_bounds.extc:19:16: note: while referencing '__extc_a'
g4_arena_bounds.extc:16:13: warning: array subscript 3 is above array bounds of 'extc_arena[2]' [-Warray-bounds=]
$ clang -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused -fsyntax-only g4_arena_bounds.c
g4_arena_bounds.extc:13:33: warning: array index 3 is past the end of the array (that has type 'extc_arena[2]') [-Warray-bounds]
   13 |             extc_arena_release(&__extc_a[3]);
$ gcc -std=c11 -O1 -g -fsanitize=address -o g4_asan g4_arena_bounds.c && ./g4_asan
==127813==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 8
    #0 ... in extc_arena_release g4_arena_bounds.c:87
    #1 ... in main g4_arena_bounds.extc:12
exit=1
NOTE: gcc -fsyntax-only does NOT report this (GCC's -Warray-bounds is a middle-end warning); the full compile is required. The warning is not a false positive: ASan reproduces the out-of-bounds read at the same site.

findings.title: An unstarted coroutine that touches the domain layer keeps its `$next` wrapper but loses the `$step` body: `-Wundefined-internal` / 'used but never defined', and a hard link error at -O0
findings.why: The coroutine section emits a `$next` wrapper for a coroutine that needs a zone (src/codegen.c:4500 declaration, :4608 definition; the call to `$step` is generated at :1906-1912), while the `$step` body is emitted as an ordinary function that the dead-definition pass may drop (the `$step` definition comes from genFunc, src/codegen.c:4460). Nothing in the two mechanisms is coupled: a coroutine that is never `ext`-started has no caller, so `$step` is dropped, but the domain layer in its body sets coroNeedsZone, so `$next` is still emitted and still calls it. gcc and clang both diagnose the dangling static, and at -O0 (where the unreferenced wrapper is not discarded) the product fails to link.
findings.trigger: A coroutine function whose body touches the domain layer (even just `let d = domain::single()`) and that is never started with `ext` from any domain block. Removing the domain reference, or actually starting the coroutine with `d.run { ext w(...) }`, makes the diagnostic disappear.

collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status

coverage_notes:
SWEEP. Corpus = every *.extc under tests/ examples/ stdlib/ bench/ (961 files). Generation: `./build/extc -w <f> -o /tmp/rev/gen/<mangled>.c` with a 25 s per-file timeout. 594 files were accepted (rc=0) and generated; 366 were rejected by the checker (mostly tests/errors/**, plus modules that need -I/sibling files: tests/real-lib/numpy.extc needs npytable, etc.); 1 timed out: stdlib/stl/hashSet.extc burned 15+ min of CPU without finishing (a real HANG, left for the perf/hang owner; two independent invocations, mine and another auditor's, both stalled there). Generated C and logs kept in /tmp/rev/gen/ and /tmp/rev/logs/.
SCAN MODES. Every one of the 594 generated files was scanned four ways: gcc -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused -fsyntax-only; clang ... -fsyntax-only; gcc ... -c -o /dev/null; clang ... -c -o /dev/null. The full-compile modes are not optional: GCC implements -Warray-bounds / -Wmaybe-uninitialized / -Wstringop-* in the middle end, so '-fsyntax-only' can never emit them (verified with a control program: gcc -fsyntax-only = 0 warnings, gcc -c -O2 = -Warray-bounds). Task step 2 named only -fsyntax-only; I ran both and report the middle-end results from the -c runs.
CORPUS RESULT (all four modes, 594 files): 9 unique diagnostics, none in the requested defect categories except one hard error. (1) stdlib/std/coro/scheduler.extc -> 'unknown type name extc_coro' (finding 1's family; the same missing-typedef class, corpus instance). (2) tests/attacks/h10_deep and tests/traps/recursion_too_deep -> -Winfinite-recursion, which is the *point* of those tests (extC's extc_rec_enter guard), not a defect. (3) tests/dyn/{dyn_in_array,dyn_shape_area} -> -Wmissing-braces (brace elision on nested aggregate initializers, no semantic effect; noise). (4) tests/instimpl/t_dyn_multi -> -Wunused-parameter (noise). No -Wuninitialized, -Wmaybe-uninitialized, -Wstringop-overflow/overread/truncation, -Wstrict-aliasing, -Wshift-*, -Wnull-dereference, -Wint-conversion, -Wincompatible-pointer-types, -Wimplicit-function-declaration (GCC 15/clang 21 both make the last two errors, so they would have been caught), -Wdiv-by-zero, -Wtautological-compare, -Woverflow or -Wformat anywhere in the corpus. The corpus being clean is why findings 1-3 and 5 were hunted with hand-written programs: they are all 'a runtime name is emitted but its definition is gated on a flag that a type-only use never sets', the same shape as the already-known `__extc_ret_v` undeclared bug, and the corpus's golden tests always exercise the value-producing form of each construct.
ALREADY-KNOWN ITEMS NOT RE-REPORTED. (a) f64 literals with integral value emitted as C integer constants (`1.0/2.0` -> `(1 / 2)`): reproduced (`double a = (1 / 2);`), left to the differential owner. (b) `__extc_ret_v` undeclared: not reproduced in the corpus; the fall-off-the-end path is handled by an extc_trapMsg noreturn call (verified for `fn f(c: bool) -> i64 { if c { return 1 } }` and an empty body), so no uninitialized-read variant was found. (c) the `__extc_a[2]` overrun in tests/ext/domain_runs.extc: NOT counted as a new root cause - finding 4 is the same blkMaxLevel/ST_DOMAIN defect, reported only because one more nesting level turns it into a genuine -Warray-bounds subscript-past-the-end with an ASan-confirmed stack-buffer-overflow, which the one-past-the-end `&__extc_a[2]` form is not. (d) EX_INDEX/EX_SLICE on a nullable ref, `mut` discarded, etc. were not re-examined.
NEGATIVE / DISMISSED PROBES (all clean or by design). Uninitialized: every `var x: T` with a zero value is emitted zeroed (`int64_t x = 0;`) and types containing references are rejected by the checker ('cannot zero-initialize') - so no -Wmaybe-uninitialized path found; the zero-value analysis does have the two coroutine/dyn holes reported above. Bounds/size: the corpus and the generated runtime were searched for fixed arrays - besides `__extc_a` only `__extc_raw_saved[256]` (clamped via sizeof), `extc_cout_buf[1<<18]` (checked before memcpy), `th[256]`/`args[256]` in extc_par_run (clamped with `if (threads > 256)`), `b[32]` for snprintf - all bounded. Division, shifts, narrowing and conversions all go through trapping helpers (extc_divI/extc_modI/extc_shiftCount/extc_narrowI/extc_narrowU) called with the correct widths (verified 8/16/32/64), which is also why -Wdiv-by-zero/-Wtautological-compare/-Wshift-* cannot fire by construction. No pointer-cast type punning exists in the generated code (only `(char *)`). Printing: the descriptor printers are fully cast (`%d`+(int), `%lld`+(long long), `%llu`+(unsigned long long), `%g`+(double), `%.*s`+(int)) - no -Wformat. gcc -fanalyzer over the corpus produced nothing on the files tried.
ORACLES THAT DID NOT HELP. EXTC_DBG_ARENA=1 and EXTC_SELFCHECK=1 exit 0 silently, including on the known-bad tests/ext/domain_runs.extc, so neither can be used to find arena-level mismatches. My independent per-function check (declared `__extc_a[N]` vs highest index used in that function) over all 594 files found exactly one file with a real overrun - tests/ext/domain_runs.extc - i.e. the domain-nesting shape is the only one the corpus exercises.
OUT OF SCOPE BUT NOTED (for the checker/parser owners). `fn take(h: coroutine<i64>)` cannot be called with a value returned by a `-> coroutine<i64>` function: 'error: argument expects `coroutine<i64>`, found `w$frame`' - the frame/handle coercion does not apply to a `let`-bound call result, which looks like a false reject. `stdlib/std/coro/scheduler.extc` generates C that mentions `extc_coro` but never drives a handle (no extc_coro_next/send/value call in the output) - possibly related to the missing-typedef bug, worth a codegen correctness look. Findings 1-3, 5 are all reproducible in /tmp/rev/genwarn/ with an EVIDENCE.txt holding every command and its full output. 另：本次扫描独立复现了两条已由别的单元报告、根因相同的缺陷（`blkMaxLevel` 漏 `ST_DOMAIN` 的升级形态 `-Warray-bounds`；`extc_convFloat` 的 `(double)INT64_MAX` 上界），为避免重复计数未列入 findings。
